Adaptive Plate: [[Category:Perks]] {{PerkTemplate | Tags = Defensive, Armor | Description = Taking an identical Type of Damage twice will activate a temporary holy bubble that grants Damage Reduction. Gain additional Damage Reduction against the specific Damage Types that triggered it. |Details = *+10% defense against all damage while the bubble is active per 1 of the perk **Uses the damageTaken/(1+defense%) formula *+40% additional defense against the damage type(s) that procced the bubble per 1 of the perk ** i.e. +50% per perk against matched types **Uses the damageTaken/(1+defense%) formula *Bubble Duration is equivalent to 3 + 2 * perkAmount seconds |Notes = *Damage reduction works on self damage and can be procced by self damage. *Damage reduction works on DoTs, but cannot be procced by DoTs. *Stores damage type taken indefinitely until death or rejoining, meaning if you got hit by two '''Physical''' attacks 30 minutes apart with no other damage taken in between, the perk would still proc on '''Physical'''. *This perk has no cooldown and can be procced again immediately after the current bubble expires. '''Explanation:''' Upon taking 2 consecutive hits from an attack with the same damage type(s) this perk activates, granting global damage reduction with additional damage reduction against attacks that deal exclusively the same damage type(s) as the one that activated the perk. i.e. If an attack dealt 2 damage types at once and that attack hit you twice successively, proccing the bubble, then the increased damage reduction only works against attacks that deal BOTH of the proccing damage types. '''True''' DMG is treated as a separate damage type, but attacks that have had their damage type(s) converted to true will not count as '''True''' DMG for this perk but will count as their original damage type(s) (despite appearing as True DMG). Additional damage reduction does not apply to constituent damage type(s) of '''Physical''' or '''Magic''' if '''Physical''' or '''Magic''' procced the perk. i.e. If '''Physical''' procced the bubble, then the additional damage reduction only works against pure '''Physical''' damage. |Preview=Adaptive Plate |Sources = Northern Innovator }}

Armor Penetration:
[[Category:Mechanics]] ==Defense==
dmgTaken =
if def% > 0, dmg / (1 + def%)
if def% < 0, dmg * (1 + |def%|)

* Positive Defense decreases incoming damage, negative defense increases incoming damage * Every unique source of defense is multiplicative to eachother, rather than additive ** Defense stats however, are additive with eachother, i.e. physical and air defense are additive when reducing air damage taken ==Armor Penetration== Where pen is a decimal, 10 armor penetration is = 0.1 pen, If defense ≤ (pen + 0.2), armor multiplier = defense - pen *If defense - pen > 0, then armor multiplier acts as positive defense **i.e. the multiplier is 1 / (1 + armor multiplier) *If defense - pen < 0, then the armor multiplier acts as negative defense **i.e. the multiplier is 1 - armor multiplier If defense > (pen + 0.2), armor multiplier = defense / (1 + 5 * pen) *Armor multiplier acts as positive defense **i.e. the multiplier is 1 / (1 + armor multiplier) ===Examples=== For example, against an enemy with 100% '''Physical Defense''' with a 10 damage '''Physical''' attack At 80 armor penetration *1 - 0.8 = 0.2 *10 / (1 + 0.2) = ~8.33 physical damage taken At 120 armor penetration *1 - 1.2 = -0.2 *10 * (1 - (-0.2)) = 12 physical damage taken At 20 armor penetration *1 / (1 + 5 * 0.2) = 0.5 *10 / (1 + 0.5) = ~6.67 physical damage taken {{Armor Penetrations}} ==Notes==
  • '''True''' Damage does not benefit from Armor Penetration, Armor Debuffs, or other Armor Reduction sources
  • Multiple sources of Armor Penetration are additive with eachother regardless of the type they negate
  • Armor loss from Armor Debuffs is also additive with Armor Penetration
  • Armor Penetration and Armor Debuffs do not apply to non-stat based defense effects, i.e. {{StatusEffects|Reinforce}}

Attack Speed: [[Category:Mechanics]] [[Category:Incomplete]] Attack Speed is the property that determines the speed that attack animations can be performed. Attack Speed can generally be divided into three types : * Weapon Attack Speed * Stat Attack Speed * Perk Attack Speed Bonuses within the same type are additive with each other, but multiplicative with the other types ===Weapon Attack Speed=== Weapon Attack Speed is the attack speed value listed on weapon parts, and is the average of both weapon parts. * i.e. [[Basic Handle]] has an Attack Speed of 1, and [[Agile Blade]] has an attack speed of 1.2, so the attack speed value of this weapon combination is equal to (1 + 1.2)/2 = 1.1 * [[Races#tabber-Kitsune|Kitsune]] adds +0.1 to this value ===Stat Attack Speed=== Stat Attack Speed is the attack speed stat found on [[Equipment]] and the [[Enchantments|Quick Enchantment]] ===Perk Attack Speed=== Perk Attack Speed is the attack speed bonuses from [[Perks]], or [[Status Effects|Buffs]] granted by perks. * For a list of related perks see [[Perks#attack_speed|Attack Speed Perks]] * [[Stone Weapon]] is a notable exception, where despite being an attack speed modifier from a perk source it isn't a part of this category, and is instead multiplicative with all attack speed types ==Application== When applying attack speed to an attack, you divide the attacks base attack time by your attack speed multiplier : * AttackTime = BaseAttackTime ÷ AttackSpeedMultiplier * AttackSpeedMultiplier = (weaponAttackSpeed × statAttackSpeedMultiplier × perkAttackSpeedMultiplier) Attack speed bonuses are applied differently depending on whether they're positive or negative. * A positive bonus of x increases attack speed by multiplying it by 1 + x * A negative bonus of x decreases attack speed by dividing it by 1 + |x| For example, a +25% bonus would result in a 1.25x multiplier, while a -25% penalty results in a 0.8x multiplier For example, if you had an attack that had a base attack time of 1, a weapon attack speed of 1.1, a stat attack speed of -25%, and two different attack speed perks that gave +10% and +20% attack speed respectively : * weaponAttackSpeed = 1.1 * statAttackSpeedMultiplier = 1 ÷ (1 + |-25%|) = 0.8 * perkAttackSpeedMultiplier = 1 + 10% + 20% = 1.3 * AttackSpeedMultiplier = 1.1 × 0.8 × 1.3 = 1.144 * AttackTime = 1 ÷ 1.144 = ~0.874 ===Attack Specific Interactions=== Not all attacks are affected by every type of attack speed bonus, or affected by attack speed in the same way. Some attacks have other restrictions or are exceptions to normal attack speed rules. For example [[Weapon Arts]] are unaffected by general Perk Attack Speed bonuses but certain Perk Attack Speed bonuses like [[Quickcast]] and [[Power Inhale]] specifically affect them. __NOTOC__

Blood Moon:
BLOOD MOON

Notification

Event Start

The moon begins moving!?
A blood moon has begun!

Event End

The moon becomes bored again...

Overview

During a Blood Moon enemies have a high chance to spawn Bloodied or Giant, becoming much stronger than usual. Bloodied mobs have increased aggro range and item drop rate, and have a high chance of dropping an item with <-->
[[File:Thirsty Enchantment.png|140px|link=Enchantments]]
[[Thirsty Enchantment| Thirsty Enchantment]]

Giant mobs have increased size (Wow) and drop much more items than usual on death. Both can drop [[Brilliant Dust]]
Activating the [[Lost_Shrine#tabber-Shrine_of_Clouds|Shrine of Clouds]] during this event will cause [[Lord Stratos (Enemy)|Lord Stratos]] to become Bloodied, gaining increased stats, new attacks, and new rewards.

Bloody/Bloodied Enemies

A blood red glow. Bloody mobs have a red colored name, and can only spawn during '''Blood Moon'''

Cooldowns: [[Category:Mechanics]] ==Cooldowns== A cooldown is a timer that prevents the use of a skill or effect until the timer has fully elapsed, Cooldown Reduction is an effect that reduces this timer. Weapon Art and Rune Cooldowns are limited to integers, and decrease every 'game tick', which will typically occur once every second. This means that cooldowns that aren't whole numbers are floored to the next whole number. * e.g. a 10.99 second cooldown becomes a 10 second cooldown. Weapon Art and Rune cooldowns can only be reduced up to a 1 second minimum. Cooldown Reduction effects can typically be divided into three categories, Cooldown Reduction, Cooldown 'Speed', and Flat Cooldown Reduction. ===Cooldown reduction list=== '''For a list of all perks and effects that provide Cooldown Reduction, ''' '''see [[Perks#cooldown_reduction|Cooldown reduction list]].''' ===Cooldown Reduction=== 'Cooldown Reduction' effects reduce the cooldown of a Weapon Art/Rune by a set percentage. Application of this type of CDR can be done like so : * FinalCD = BaseCD * (1 - CooldownReduction%) Notable perks/effects of this type include the following : * [[Races#tabber-Elf|Elf]] * [[Races#tabber-High_Elf|High Elf]] * [[Channeled Weapon]] * [[Divinity]] * [[Magic Surge]] * [[Mageling Spirit]] ===Cooldown Speed=== Cooldown 'Speed' effects apply similarly to normal Cooldown Reduction effects, but follow a diminishing curve for its effectiveness. Termed as 'cooldown speed' because it can be represented as increasing the effective time elapsed per game tick. Application of this type of CDR can be calculated with the following formula : * FinalCD = BaseCD / (1 + CooldownSpeed%) * e.g. at +50% Cooldown Speed, a 10 second cooldown would become a 6.66 second cooldown. Though due to game ticks, the cooldown is actually reduced to 6 seconds. Notable perks/effects of this type include the following : * [[Caster]] * [[Emotional]] * [[Mage Rage]] * [[Poison Acceleration]] * [[Runic Winds]] * [[Star Friendship]] * [[Wave Rider]] * [[Whirlwind]] ===Flat Cooldown Reduction=== Flat Cooldown Reduction effects reduce the cooldown of a Weapon Art/Rune by a flat second amount. Due to cooldowns being unable to be reduced in decimal amounts, these effects instead will only activate after it accumulating to an integer, i.e. 1 second. *e.g. [[Shamanic Flow]] at 1 perk amount will only take effect every 2 hits. Notable perks/effects of this type include the following : * [[Shamanic Flow]] * [[Power Surge]] ===Other Cooldown Effects=== While there are three main categories of cooldown reduction effects, there are also cooldown increases, and effects that set the base cooldown to a different value. Cooldown Increases increase the cooldown of an effect by a set amount or percent, notable examples of this include the following : * [[Voltaic Body]] There are also effects that change the base cooldown to a different value. Examples of these perks/effects include the following : * [[Draconic Blood]] * [[Heat Drill]] * [[Gladiatorial Rage]] A distinction from other cooldown reduction/increase effects is important here, as some perks use the base cooldown of an effect for their own effects. ==Examples== It should also be noted that different sources of Cooldown Reduction, and Cooldown Speed are multiplicative with each other. * e.g. When you have more than one source of Cooldown Reduction, or Cooldown Speed they are applied like so : * FinalCD = BaseCD * (1 - cooldownReductionA%) * (1 - cooldownReductionB%) / (1 + cooldownSpeedC%) / (1 + cooldownSpeedD%) For a practical example, a build with [[Races#tabber-High_Elf|High Elf]], 3 [[Channeled Weapon]], 1 [[Caster]], and 1 [[Whirlwind]] using [[Weapon_Arts#storm_stomp|Storm Stomp]], which has a 20 second base cooldown. * BaseCD * (Channeled Weapon) * (High Elf) / (Caster) / (Whirlwind) * 20 * (1 - (20% + 5%*3)) * (1 - 25%) / (1 + 10%) / (1 + 30%) = 6.81818181818, which is rounded to a 6 second cooldown. {{Cooldowns}}

Critical Hit:
[[Category:Mechanics]] [[Category:Incomplete]] A '''Critical Hit''' is a type of hit that multiplies its damage by its critical damage multiplier. A critical hit is indicated by a brighter text-outline on the damage indicator. ===Critical Chance=== Critical Chance is influenced by the users Dexterity Boost and a variety of perks. Perks and effects that increase critical chance or influence whether an effect is a critical or not can be divided into two categories, effects that influence your "Natural Critical Chance", and effects that don't influence natural critical chance. A "Natural Critical Hit" is one sourced from your natural critical chance, the distinction is made because certain effects scale with your natural critical chance or only activate on natural critical hits. Effects/Perks that contribute to Natural Critical Chance contain the following :
  • Dexterity Boost (increases critical chance at a rate of 10:1)
  • [[Flowing Crits]]
  • [[Seismic Momentum]]
  • [[Spell Slinger (Perk)|Spell Slinger]]
  • [[Sharp Crits]]
  • {{StatusEffects|Perfection}} ([[Perfection]])
  • [[Heightened Reflexes]]
Natural Critical chance can not be negatively affected by proc coefficient, but can be positively affected. * i.e. an attack with 0 proc coefficient has the same chance to crit as an attack with 1 proc coefficient, and an attack with 2 proc coefficient has double the critical chance of an attack with 1 proc coefficient Effects/Perks that influence whether you crit or not, but are not natural critical hits/do not increase natural critical chance are the following :
  • {{StatusEffects|Critical Boost}}
  • [[Venom Eater]]
  • [[Thief Training]]
  • [[Carrying Winds]]
  • {{StatusEffects|King's Luck}} ([[Caci King Spirit]])
Notably these effects that increase critical chance are not additive with natural critical chance, but instead a separate critical roll. * i.e. with 20% natural critical chance, and 20% critical chance from [[Carrying Winds]], the chance for a hit to crit is equal to 1 - (1 - 20%) * (1 - 20%) = 36% instead of 40% ===Critical Damage=== Critical hits cause hits to deal more damage compared to a non-critical hit, the magnitude of which is determined by the critical damage multiplier. The base critical damage multiplier is 150% (1.5x), and can be increased or decreased by a variety of perks and effects. Critical Damage is increased directly by the players natural critical chance *i.e. Critical Damage Multiplier is equal to 1 + 50% + naturalCriticalChance To see a list of perks that increase critical damage see [[Perks#crit_damage|Perks]]

Currency: [[Category:Mechanics]] '''Currency''' in voxlblade can be divided in to two main types, Voxos (V$) and SP. Voxos are a resource gained by doing quests, killing mobs, completing dungeons and selling items at shops, the player is only able to have up to 100,000 V$ at once. Shop buildings have a V$ icon above their door, and the "DESTROY" button in the users inventory changes to "SELL" while in a shop. Voxos can be used to buy armor, upgrade gear, transfer enchants, and as a trading fee. Every trade has a fee of at least 25V$, and an additional 1/3rd of the traded items sell value. SP is a resource gained by leveling up (+5 SP), completing [[Dungeons#Daily_Challenges|Daily Challenges]] (+5 SP), completing certain quests (+1 SP), leveling up crafting (+1 SP), and defeating legendary mobs (+1 SP). SP is used to [[Weapons|upgrade your sword]], transfer [[Brokkr|certain types of weapons between slots]], or learn guild [[Cantrips]]. All SP spent is refunded upon using the [[Lost_Shrine#tabber-Shrine_of_Regret|Shrine of Regret]], and all SP spent on handles is refunded upon joining the [[Monk|Monk Guild]]

Damage Calculation:
[[Category:Mechanics]] [[Category:Incomplete]] {{Delay}}
DMG =
Base Damage
× Effective Boost Multiplier
× Level Bonus Multiplier
× Damage Bonus Multiplier
× Damage Reduced Multiplier
× Damage Type Multiplier
× Type Specific Multiplier
× Crit Multiplier
× Armor Multiplier
  • Base Damage is the base damage of the source
  • Effective Boost Multiplier is the damage bonus from [[Damage Type and Scalings|Scaling]]
  • Level Bonus Multiplier is the damage bonus from [[Mechanics#Levels|Level]]
  • Damage Bonus Multiplier is the product of multiplying all damage bonuses from perks & other effects together.
  • Damage Reduced Multiplier is the multiplier for how much damage is reduced by damage reducing effects, e.g. {{StatusEffects|Weakness}}, [[Cursed Flames]], [[Pursuit]], etc.
  • Damage Type Multiplier is the damage type of the attack, and perk/effect damage type bonuses that apply to the attack, see [[Damage Type and Scalings]] for more information
  • Type Specific Multipliers are perks/effects that only apply to certain or specific damage types, e.g. {{StatusEffects|Rage}}, {{StatusEffects|Sticky}}, [[Photosynthesis]], etc.
  • Crit Multiplier refers to the critical damage multiplier, and any increases to it from perks or other effects, see [[Critical Hit]] for more information
  • Armor Multiplier refers to enemy armor such as [[Stats|Water Defense]], and armor reducing effects such as {{StatusEffects|Shatter}}, see [[Armor Penetration]] for more information
Typically the order in which bonuses are applied does not matter towards final damage dealt, however certain perks and effects are only affected by certain stages, or only consider up to specific stages when calculating their own damage. Some notable perks/effects of this type contain the following :
  • {{StatusEffects|Lightning Cloak}}
  • {{StatusEffects|Cloudpush}}
  • {{StatusEffects|Cinderpull}}
  • {{StatusEffects|Luminescent}}
  • [[Blub Blub]]
  • [[Fractured Energy]]
  • [[Fungal Prototype]]
  • [[Phantom Pain]]
  • [[Explosive Charge]]
  • [[Ichor Spark]] (Chain Lightning)
  • [[Storm Rend]] (Chain Lightning)
  • [[Curse Rip]]
  • [[Honey Gather]]
Damage Type and Scalings:
[[Category:Mechanics]]
'''Damage Scaling(s)''' are what determines the boosts an attack scales off of. Damage Type is the output of your damage. '''Damage Type''' and Damage Scaling are completely independent of eachother. ==='''Damage Scaling'''=== * '''Damage Scalings''' multiply the corresponding boost stat to obtain effective boost * In the cases of multiple scalings, they are all additive with eachother * For example on an attack with, at 1.1 '''Air''' Scaling with +50% '''Air''' Boost, and 0.5 '''Magic''' Scaling with +25% '''Magic''' Boost, the total effective boost would be 1.1 * 50% + 0.5 * 25% = 67.5% * To apply this value to our attack, we add a constant 1 to obtain our multiplier, using the numbers from our previous example would look like this :
** dmg * (1 + (1.1 * 50%) + (0.5 * 25%))
** dmg * (1 + 67.5%) ==='''Damage Type'''=== * '''Damage Type''' determines how damage is distributed. It uses the total damage and multiplies it by your damage type. * For example, let's say your total damage is 100. If you had the damage types of 0.7 '''Fire''', and 0.3 '''Earth''', the attack would deal 70 '''fire''' damage and 30 '''earth''' damage. If you had +3 [[Channeled Weapon]] adding 0.15 '''Magic''' Type to this attack, it would deal an additional 15 '''magic''' damage. * Damage Types don't always add up to 1.0 * Damage Types have NOTHING to do with scaling

  • Grants {{StatusEffects|Draconic Infusion}} at 0.1 * perkAmount potency for 20 seconds

  • All attacks gain +0.1 damage type of your respective draco color per 0.1 buff potency
    • if you are not [[Races#tabber-Dragon_Blooded|Dragon Blooded]], instead gain physical damage type.
    • Does not apply to attacks without proc coefficient

      • Chance to apply burn is affected by proc coefficient.
    • Hex: Increases applied debuff potency by 5% and duration by 15% per 1 of this perk

    • Water: Become immune to debuffs, and release a pulse every 8 - 1 * perkAmount seconds that heals and cleanses
      • Pulse base Heal is equal to 0.1
        • 1.0 Water scaling
        • Can proc healing related effects
    • Earth: Increases Poise damage dealt by 15% and Stun Resistance by 0.15 per 0.1 {{StatusEffects|Draconic Infusion}} potency
===Dragon Bubble=== * Dragon Bubble Base Damage is equal to 20 + 2 * perkAmount ** 1.0 Damage Type of the users Draconic Color ** 1.0 Scaling of the users Draconic Color ** Base Healing (Holy) is equal to 4 + 0.4 * perkamount ** Base Healing (Water) is equal to 1.538 + 0.1538 * perkamount ** Can proc other effects ** Base Poise Damage is equal to 45 ** Base Cooldown of 7 seconds ** Does not collide with objects, but detonates immediately upon contact with an enemy |Notes = * Damage Type and Scalings of abilities depends on your skin color as a [[Races#tabber-Dragon_Blooded|Dragon Blooded]] ** (1) Red is Fire, (2) White is Air, (3) Green is Earth, (4) Blue is Water, (5) Yellow is Holy, (6) Purple is Hex **If you are not Dragon Blooded the type is '''Physical''' * Affected by [[Perk Effectiveness]] ===Attack Stats===

    • Random debuffs can be any of the following :

    • {{StatusEffects|Slowness}} at 0.2 potency

*'''The Great One?'''

Enchantments:
[[Category:Enchantment]]
Occasionally, when a piece of equipment is obtained, it will have a bonus effect on it, listing text next to its name and providing extra stats.

Although rare, equipment can have multiple enchants on them, up to 3 per piece.

Equipment with two enchants are called 'double enchants' and for three enchants, 'triple enchants'.

Enchanted items are obtained by the same method you get the item normally, such as buying, crafting, or as a drop from an enemy.

Certain enchantments can only be obtained from a specific type of modified enemy, or specific dungeon:
* Corrupt - from corrupt enemies, indicated by glowing purple particles, only possible in the overworld.
* Legendary - from legendary enemies, indicated by glowing yellow particles, only possible in the overworld.
* Thirsty - from bloody enemies, indicated by glowing red particles, only possible in the overworld during a blood moon event.
* Corroded - from the Lord Frogg dungeon rewards at the end of the dungeon.
* Sweet - from the Queen Bumblz Hive dungeon rewards at the end of the dungeon.

Legendary and Corrupt enchants cannot be in a double or triple enchant, but the other exclusive enchants can be.



Additionally, enchants can also be obtained by using a [[Cleansing Tear]] while having equipment with the Corrupt enchant equipped, this method has an increased chance to yield an item with multiple enchants on it.

Enchants can be upgraded for 1 [[Brilliant Gem]] by talking to [[Brokkr]], with ascended enchants providing different effects. Trying to upgrade an ascended enchant will return it back to its default form.

==Enchant Transferring==
You can transfer enchants from one item to another through the enchant transfer machine in [[Magus]], found near [[Lapis]].

To use, select an ''unenchanted'' item you want to put the enchant on, and then select an item with the enchant you want to transfer. Then press the confirm button to transfer the enchant. Single-enchants will have a fee of 2000 V$.

Double or triple enchants will instead cost 5000 V$ and a [[Refined Core]] with a 33% chance of successful transfer. If the transfer fails, it will only consume the Voxos and the refined core without transferring the enchant. The transfer is guaranteed to succeed on the 4th attempt.

Enemy Modifiers:
[[Category:Mechanics]]
==Overview==
Every mob (With the exception of Bosses) has a slight chance to spawn with a modifier, indicated by a variety of colored particles emitting from them.

Each variant boasts increased damage, health, tenacity, and special loot drops.

Keep in mind that guaranteed enchant/armor drops can be nullified by [[Trophy Hunter]]

Modifiers are half as likely to happen in [[Frontier Village]] and twice as likely to happen in the [[Deadlands]] and [[Icy Plateau]]

==List of Modifiers==
===Magical===
A mystical blue glow. Magical mobs have a blue colored name.

Special Properties:
*Guaranteed chance to drop an [[Enchantments|enchanted]] armor piece

[[File:Magical Enemy.png|300px]]

===Corrupted===
A dark purple glow. Corrupted mobs have a purple colored name, and have a much higher chance of spawning during the [[Encroaching Void]] event.

Special Properties:
*High chance to drop [[Binded Corruption]]
*High chance to drop [[Enchantments|Corrupt Enchantment]]

[[File:Corrupt Enemy.png|300px]]

A blood red glow. Bloody mobs have a red colored name, and can only spawn during [[Blood Moon]] events.

*High chance for the item to have [[Enchantments|Thirsty Enchantment]]
*Low chance to drop [[Brilliant Dust]]

*Guaranteed chance to drop [[Brilliant Dust]]

[[File:Legendary Enemy.png|300px]]

==Giant Enemies==
Enemies can very rarely spawn as Giant, increasing their size, damage, tenacity, and health. The chance is greatly increased during the [[Blood Moon]]. Giant enemies drop more items than usual upon being defeated, and can also drop [[Brilliant Dust]].

There are three tiers of Giant enemies: Big, Colossal and Titanic, with stats and drops increasing accordingly.

[[File:Giant Enemies.png|800px]]

Colossal and Titanic enemies trigger a message in the chat when they spawn or are killed. They also feature boss health bars that show when you are close enough.

Giant enemies can have normal modifiers alongside their Giant trait, if the enemy features a boss health bar, the color of the respective modifier will show there as well.

Additionally giant enemies have an increased chance to drop enchants depending on their tier:
* 1.5x for Big enemies
* 2x for Colossal enemies
* 3x for Titanic enemies

Forge:
[[Category:Mechanics]] '''Forges''' are anvils used to upgrade [[Equipment]] for [[Currency|Voxos]]. Equipment can be upgraded up to a maximum of 5 times, with each upgrade costing more Voxos than the last. Each upgrade costs 500V$, 1,500V$, 2,000V$, 3,000V$, 4,000V$, respectively up to a total of 11,000V$ required to upgrade an equipment piece to its maximum. Upgrading an equipment increases positive stats and negative stats using the following formula :
  • if Stat is positive, stat * (1 + upgradeLevel/10)
  • if Stat is negative, stat / (1 + upgradeLevel/10)
Forges can be found at the following locations, and also be summoned via the [[Knight]] guild [[Cantrips#tabber-Summon_Anvil|Summon Anvil Cantrip]]
  • [[Frontier Village]]
  • [[Bogtown]]
  • [[Cloudlands]]
  • [[Knights Outpost]]
  • [[Ice Caverns#Map|Ice Caverns]]

Guilds:
'''Guilds''' are a method of enhancing your character in Voxlblade, typically obtained by talking to the guild NPC after meeting a level and reputation requirement. Guilds provide stat boosts and [[perks]], which are strengthened upon guild promotion, accomplished via doing the guild promotion quests. Guilds also each have a [[Cantrips|cantrip]], nearly all of which can be unlocked from their respective Guild NPC after reaching rank 2 for SP. [[File:The Ice Caverns.png|950px|center|link=]]
Deep ice caverns inhabited by The Northern Kingdom
A mining site and passageway for the Northern Kingdom that has been overrun by the void, housing many dangerous mobs. Many Knights and Miners are also stranded within, due to their exit elevator lacking power. The player must help [[Captain Eksha]] find the Power Cores for the elevator by bringing dynamite to areas sealed off by rubble. However, all three Power Cores are being held by the powerful boss enemies: [[Delta-Spider (Enemy)|Delta-Spider]], [[Omega-Batty (Enemy)|Omega-Batty]] and [[Proto-Mungus (Enemy)|Proto-Mungus]]. Complete the dungeon by successfully powering the elevator and talking to Captain Eksha. =='''Map'''== {{Map:Tundra_Dungeon}} =='''Intensity'''== This dungeon has a feature called Intensity, which will increase the longer you stay. Every so often, an Intensity Event occurs, with the potency being based off how high the intensity is. Mobs:
'''Mobs''' are any living creature with a health bar that can attack.

Mobs can be encountered in a majority of locations within the overworld and dungeons. Upon killing any mob you are awarded with EXP and Voxos, with most Mobs dropping [[Equipment]] or materials used for [[Crafting]].

Mobs may come with a [[Enemy_Modifiers|Modifier]] that enhances their stats. This can occur randomly or during certain [[Events]].

The Bestiary lists every single non-event mob in the game. Giving the mob lore and bounty rewards based on how many of that specific mob you have defeated.
Every mob comes with 4 bounties, with the third bounty reward being a unique [[Equipment]] for each mob. A [[Titles|Title]] relating to the mob is given as the last reward.

Upon completing all four bestiary bounties for any mob, you are able to loop their unique bounty equipment to reobtain it with the same amount of kills required.

Some rare strong mobs are classified as minibosses and have a '''single''' guaranteed spawn every 30 minutes in a server.

  • {{StatusEffects|Shatter}} (0.2 potency)
  • {{StatusEffects|Bleed}}
  • {{StatusEffects|Burn}}
  • {{StatusEffects|Poison}}
  • {{StatusEffects|Slowness}} (0.2 potency)

==Additional Notes== Unlocked via the [https://www.roblox.com/game-pass/36304796/Ork Ork gamepass] for 50 robux. |-|High Elf= {{Race |Race Name = HIGH ELF |Image = High Elf1.png, High Elf2.png, High Elf3.png, High Elf4.png, High Elf5.png, High Elf6.png |Race Description = The High Elves are consisted of the upper echelon of the elven tribes, They are known to be rude and respect only those who are the same status. The provided cooldown reduction does not have diminishing returns and directly applies a multiplier of x0.75 to weapon art cooldowns.

==Additional Notes== Unlocked via the [https://www.roblox.com/game-pass/36304752/High-Elf High Elf gamepass] for 50 robux. |-|Arborian= {{Race |Race Name = ARBORIAN |Image = Arborian1.png, Arborian2.png, Arborian3.png, Arborian4.png, Arborian5.png, Arborian6.png |Race Description = The Arborians are druidic in nature. They are trees made of tough bark and use their power to protect all life |Race Passive = -50% Fire Defense, +15 Protection, passive regen that is boosted in the sun, and a chance to entangle foes on hit. }} ==Passive Details==

Healing whilst in sun is 0.41% per second.

Attacks have a 5% chance to entangle enemies for 1 second, which deals 2 earth damage, 50 poise damage and prevents the enemy from attacking or moving.

Entangle damage does not scale with level but scales with any other damage boost or debuff.

You can still regenerate in the darkness, but at a reduced rate.

Being [[Vampire]] will cause you to regenerate in the darkness at the full rate, but regenerate in the sunlight at a reduced rate.

==Additional Notes== Unlocked via the [https://www.roblox.com/game-pass/36304725/Arborian Arborian gamepass] for 50 robux. They posess incredible speed and reflex and are not often caught by surprise. |Race Passive = Gain +2 Jump Boost and 10% Movement Speed and +0.1 to your attack speed. }} ==Passive Details==

Gain +2 Jump Boost and 10% Movement Speed and +0.1 to your weapon attack speed.

The attack speed bonus is additive to your weapons innate attack speed.

==Additional Notes== Unlocked via the [https://www.roblox.com/game-pass/36304859/Kitsune Kitsune gamepass] for 50 robux. |-|Bunikin= {{Race |Race Name = BUNIKIN |Image = Bunikin1.png, Bunikin2.png, Bunikin3.png, Bunikin4.png, Bunikin5.png, Bunikin6.png |Race Description = The mysterious bunikin are being of mystical whimsy and are rarely seen anywhere in the world |Race Passive = Gain +5 Jump Boost and Gain dodge chance based on Jump Boost, when you dodge with the passive you gain a 100% chance to crit for one attack. }} ==Passive Details==

The passive dodge chance is not affected by [[Lucky]] perk.

Seasonal Events:
'''Seasonal Events''' are limited-time in-game events that typically occur around holidays, introducing new [[Cosmetics|Cosmetic Equipment]]!

==[[Easter Event 2023]]==
The 2023 Easter Event was launched on 4/10/2023 and introduced many different egg themed cosmetics, obtainable by defeating [[Easter Buni (Enemy)|Easter Bunis]] a new mob that randomly spawned in place of any [[Enemies]] during the event.

==[[Halloween Event 2023]]==
The 2023 Halloween Event was launched on 10/28/2023 and lasted until 11/19/2023, introducing many different Halloween themed cosmetics. These cosmetics were mostly obtainable via purchase for [[Candy Corn]], which dropped from Halloween variant enemies, [[Grumpkin (Enemy)|Grumpkin]] any mob during a [[Hallow Moon]] and [[Dungeons]] during the event.

==[[Easter Event 2024]]==
The 2024 Easter Event was launched on 4/14/2024 and introduced many different egg themed cosmetics, obtained by being found around the map or completing certain tasks.

==[[Halloween Event 2024]]==
The 2024 Halloween Event was launched on 10/31/2024 and lasted until 12/7/2024, introducing many different Halloween themed cosmetics. These cosmetics were mostly obtainable via purchase for [[Candy Corn]], which dropped from Halloween variant enemies, [[Grumpkin (Enemy)|Grumpkin]] any mob during a [[Hallow Moon]] and [[Dungeons]] during the event.

==[[Voxlmas Event 2025]]==
The 2025 Voxlmas Event was launched on 1/18/2025 and lasted until 2/23/2025, introducing many different Christmas themed cosmetics. These cosmetics were mostly obtained from Voxlmas Presents, purchasable at [[Frontier Village]] for [[Voxlmas Spirit]]. Which dropped from enemies during [[Snoestorm]]s, Voxlmas variant enemies, [[Dungeons]], or landing throws with a [[Throwable Snoeball]]

==[[Halloween Event 2025]]==
The 2025 Halloween Event was launched on 11/8/2025 and lasted until 12/26/2025, introducing many Halloween themed cosmetics, and a [[THE HALLOW SOUL (Enemy)|new boss]]. These cosmetics were mostly obtainable via purchase for [[Candy Corn]], which dropped from Halloween variant enemies, [[Grumpkin (Enemy)|Grumpkin]], [[THE HALLOW SOUL (Enemy)|The Hallow Soul]], any mob during a [[Hallow Moon]] and dungeons during the event.

==[[Easter Event 2026]]==
The 2026 Easter Event was launched on 6/11/2026 and is currently still ongoing, introducing many different egg themed cosmetics, obtained by being found around the map or completing certain tasks.

Status Effects:
[[Category:Mechanics]] '''Status Effects''' are various types of effects that are applied to your character, enemies, or allies. Status Effects have a duration, which determines the length of time the effects will last. And a Potency, which determines the strength of its effects. Duration is indicated by the number at the top of the status icon marked in seconds, and potency is indicated by the number at the bottom of the status icon. Status effects are divided into three types, Buffs, Debuffs, and Neutral status effects. These can be differentiated via the color of the status potency indicator, being green, red, and white respectively. Status Effects do not stack their potency or duration, and a player/mob can only apply one instance of a status effect to a target at a time. Status Effects use the highest potency, and duration of the applied status to determine their potency and duration.
  • e.g. if a player were to apply {{StatusEffects|Regen}} at 0.2 potency for 20 seconds, and then apply {{StatusEffects|Regen}} at 1 potency for 2 seconds, Regen will be at 1 potency for 20 seconds.
However if a status effect is applied by multiple sources onto the same player/mob, the duration of each application is respected when determining at what potency an effect applies.
  • e.g. if player A. were to apply {{StatusEffects|Regen}} at 0.2 potency for 20 seconds, and player B. were to apply {{StatusEffects|Regen}} at 1 potency for 5 seconds, then Regen will function at 1 potency for 5 seconds, and at 0.2 potency for the remaining 15.
  • Damage over Time statuses like {{StatusEffects|Bleed}}, {{StatusEffects|Burn}}, and {{StatusEffects|Poison}} instead stack per source, i.e. player A. and player B. can both apply {{StatusEffects|Bleed}} and each instance of the status will do damage separately
When the source of a status effect dies, the status effect will expire, regardless of remaining duration.

Summons: [[Category:Mechanics]] Summons are allied mobs summoned by the player. ==Summon Stats== Summons have separate stats from the player, and scale their strength with the player's level and summon boost stat. A summons max HP and Damage are equal to the following, provided no other influence from perks or other effects : *Base * (1 + summonBoost * (1 + level/80)) **Where Base is equal to the Base HP of the mob, or the Base Damage of the attack in question Summon max HP remains static from summoning, any effect that influences summon max HP will only apply when a minion is summoned. * i.e. when summoning at 100% summon boost, the summoned mobs max HP will remain the same even when swapping equipment to a set with 150% summon boost, or 50% summon boost. Summon damage scales with the players current summon boost, but only up to the amount of summon boost the player had when the minion was summoned. * i.e. when summoning at 100% summon boost, the summoned mobs damage will remain unchanged when swapping equipment to a set with 150% summon boost, but will be reduced when swapping equipment to a set with 50% summon boost Summons also have other stats, like tenacity and defense boosts. These are typically inherent to the mob itself, but can also be influenced by certain perks. ==Summon Decay== Summons also possess decay, losing a percentage of their HP per second. The decay rate of a minion is determined by the minions source, i.e. what perk/item summoned the minion, and the users summon boost. Summon Decay% = baseDecay/(1+summonBoost%) The following is a list of the base decay value for each "summon source" {| class="wikitable" style="text-align:center;" ! Source !! Decay% |- | [[Possession]] || 1.5% |- | [[Spore Trooper]] || 1% |- | [[Croakernaut Rune]] || 2% |- | [[Pack Leader Rune]] || 4% |- | [[Sporeling Toss Rune]] || 2% |- | [[Swarm Rune]] || 2% |- | [[Weapon_Arts#blessedlings_summon|Blessedlings Summon]] || 2% |- | [[Weapon_Arts#mage_bomber_summon|Mage Bomber Summon]] || 3% |- | [[Weapon_Arts#skeletal_woof_summon|Skeletal Woof Summon]] || 1% |- | [[Weapon_Arts#toaladin_summon|Toaladin Summon]] || 1% |- | [[Weapon_Arts#undead_buni_summon|Undead Buni Summon]] || 2% |- | [[Weapon_Arts#infernal_legion|Infernal Legion]] || 5% |} Summon decay remains static from summoning, any effect that influences summon decay will only apply when a minion is summoned. Additionally, [[Sacrificial Summoning]] reduces summon decay, while [[Trusty Servant]] removes it from affected summons. ==Summon Perk Interaction== Summons are separate from the player, and do not receive benefits from their perks unless stated otherwise. * e.g. [[Smoldering]] will not provide a 20% damage bonus to summons, but they obviously receive the benefits of [[Sweet Tooth]], and can be buffed by [[Inspiration]] or [[Blessing]] Certain summon perks only apply to summons when they are spawned, while other perks apply to summons adaptively. Summons can only receive healing and buffs from the summoner. A player can have a maximum of 15 summons summoned at once, this limit can be increased with [[Swarm]], or limited to a single summon with [[Trusty Servant]] For a list of summon related perks, see [[Perks#summoner|Summoner]]

Temperature:
[[Category:Mechanics]] When in a hot or cold location, the player will gain negative effects based on their temperature, indicated by a meter above the health bar visible in these locations. The temperature of the player, and the severity of the negative effects increases based on time spent in these locations.
While in hot locations gain {{StatusEffects|Sweating}} which increases damage taken by up to 70% based on the players current temperature, while in cold locations gain {{StatusEffects|Cold}} which reduces damage dealt by up to 25% based on the players current temperature.
When the temperature indicator points fully towards the right or left, the player will gain either {{StatusEffects|Overheating}} or {{StatusEffects|Freezing}} respectively. {{StatusEffects|Overheating}} causes the player to take 2% of their maximum HP per second as half true damage and half fire damage, while {{StatusEffects|Freezing}} instead causes players to take 2% of their maximum HP per second as half true damage and half air damage. These effects will no longer deal damage if the player is below 10% of their maximum HP.
All of the effects of temperature can be nullified by {{StatusEffects|Heating}} for cold biomes and {{StatusEffects|Cooling}} for hot biomes respectively.
The following locations are a list of the "hot and cold" locations present in-game * [[Caci Field]] * [[Deadlands]] * [[Icy Plateau]] * [[Ice Caverns]] (Cold Modifier)

The Bumblz Hive:
{{Delay}} [[File:Bumblz Hive Elevator.png|600px|center|Starting Elevator Area|link=]] The hive of Her Majesty [[Queen Bumblz (Enemy)|Queen Bumblz]]. This is a roguelike dungeon where you go through 3 randomly generated Floors full of [[Drone (Enemy)|Drone]]s, [[Bumblz (Enemy)|Bumblz]] and [[Bomber (Enemy)|Bomber]]s. You can enrage Queen Bumblz by hitting the totems near every floor exit 20 times until the eyes turn red. The effect will stack. This increases the overall difficulty of the dungeon and changes the loot pool. =='''Map Variation'''==
[[File:Bumblz Hive Honey Station.png|400x200px|right|thumb|Honey Station|link=]]
The entire dungeon is procedurally generated except for the tile below the elevator that spawns with a guaranteed Honey Station. Honey Stations heal 12 HP and can be consumed up to 5 times. Honey Stations have a chance to spawn in the middle of any other tiles.

Tiles also have a chance to spawn with a Chest that can drop one of the following items:
[[File:Bumblz Hive Chest.png|200px|center|thumb|Chest|link=]]
*[[Bumblz Honey Vial]] *[[Bumblzbomb Core]] *[[Drone Metal]] *[[Pollen]] *[[Health Potion]] *[[Throwable Healing Potion]] *[[Amethyst]] *[[Diamond (Item)|Diamond]] *[[Emerald]] *[[Ruby]] *[[Sapphire]]

The exit elevator randomly spawns anywhere in the dungeon. In multiplayer, players can see the elevator marked with a neon blue arrow when any player stands on it. All players have to be present on the exit to leave, it automatically teleports everybody after standing on it for 90 seconds uninterrupted. [[File:Bumblz Hive Exit.png|300px|center|thumb|Exit Elevator|link=]] =='''Dungeon Enemies'''==

=='''Enraged Modifier'''== Once a Totem is damaged 20 times its eyes turn red, increasing EXP and Voxos drop by 50% and increasing HP and Damage of all mobs by 16% per totem enraged. This boost is additive with the difficulty modifier.

Weapons: '''Weapons''' are means of attacking hostile mobs in Voxlblade. As the game title implies, most weapons are mainly swords and their variations. The weapon construction system allow the player to mix and match different tiers and types of handles and blades together to come up with entirely new weapon. You can obtain Weapon Parts by upgrading existing ones with [[Currency|SP]], completing certain [[Quests]], from [[Dungeons]] and Bosses or from opening [[Astral Present]]s and [[Brilliant Present]]s. Some perks will allow the player to [[Dual Wielding|dual wield their weapons]], change it to a [[Duelist Stance|rapier]] or even a [[Saw Stance|chainsaw]]. This can be also foregone entirely with the [[Monk]] guild, replacing handles and blades with '''Gloves''' and '''Essences'''. Another exception being the [[Blaster Ring]] giving the player the ability to use an additional ranged weapon. Combining both the [[Blaster Ring]] and [[Monk]] guild will replace the player weapon entirely with double blasters or a rifle. == '''Weapon Construction''' == When constructing a weapon at a Sword Shrine, the player is able to pick a '''Handle''' and a '''Blade''' of their choosing.
